title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, timeouts
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: under mixed-priority workloads the continuous-batcher scheduler could allow long-tail queueing and transient starvation for lower-priority routes. This PR refactors the scheduling/queueing code to improve fairness without regressing p50 throughput for high-priority workloads. Key changes: 1) move from simple round-robin cohorting to a weighted deficit-style queue that supports dynamic weight adjustment by route priority and observed latency SLA; 2) add an aging (priority boost) mechanism to prevent starvation of long-waiting requests; 3) introduce adaptive request-level timeouts and queuing time caps that are tuned by observed seq-length and model kernels to avoid wasted GPU work; 4) expose three new knobs on continuous_batcher config (max_queue_time_ms, aging_boost_window_ms, priority_weight_scale) with safe defaults tuned from cluster traces; 5) improve KV-cache interaction by ensuring warm-cache requests get scheduling preference and by instrumenting cache-hit latency to inform batching window decisions; 6) tests, perf benchmarks, and docs. This description includes design rationale, configuration guidance, and rollout plan. See commits and CI summary below.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Nice refactor. Two asks: (1) can we limit maintenance allocations to avoid oscillation under bursty traffic? (author reply: added rate limiter and included explanation in scheduler.py comments), (2) add a unit test simulating sustained low-priority traffic (author reply: added queueing_test.py with deterministic fake clock).

Lena Zhou: The default aging boost looks aggressive for small models — can we cap by model footprint? (author reply: implemented a scale factor based on average token cost and added a config cap priority_weight_scale).

benchmarks: Cluster perf: measured on a 32-GPU staging pool with mixed routes (50% high-priority short-seq, 50% low-priority long-seq). Result: p95 latency for low-priority requests improved by 22% under load (with aging boost) while high-priority p95 increased by <3% and overall token throughput increased 5-8% depending on model. CPU overhead on the scheduler path increased by ~1.4% in microbenchmarks. Detailed numbers in tools/perf/benchmarks/continuous_batcher_latency.py output included in CI artifacts.
rollout_plan: Canary on Dedicated pool: enable feature flag continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2 for 5% of traffic for 48h, monitor metrics: queue_time_histogram, starving_requests_count, model_p95_by_route; expand to 25% if no regressions, then 100% with config defaults. If high-priority p95 > configured SLO for 15m, auto-fallback to scheduler_v1 via rollback script in console/rollout_scripts.
release_notes:
- Improved continuous-batcher scheduler to reduce queueing starvation and total p95 for mixed-priority workloads.
- New config knobs: max_queue_time_ms, aging_boost_window_ms, priority_weight_scale (safe defaults).
- KV-cache warm requests now prioritized by default.
- Performance: up to 22% p95 improvement for lower-priority long-request workloads in staging benchmarks.
- No breaking changes for API consumers, but ops may tune new knobs for specific clusters.
notes_from_author: This PR focuses on scheduler correctness and a conservative set of defaults. We intentionally avoided aggressive batching window increases because those regressed latency for short-seq routes. Follow-ups: 1) auto-tuning service to adapt priority_weight_scale per fleet, 2) hybrid kernel-aware batching that factors model kernel warmup costs.
